title: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor
content:
Meta has acquired Conductor, an AI coding startup that allows users to spin up software projects by deploying multiple agents into parallel workspaces.
The news was originally reported by Axios, and Conductor shared news of its acquisition on its blog.
“I have big news: Conductor is joining Meta,” wrote the startup’s founder and CEO, Charlie Holtz, on Wednesday. “We have some big, crazy plans for the next interface,” he added, teasing that the company would have “something new” for customers to use by “early next year.”
On X, Holtz also noted that he was looking forward to working with Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, and Nat Friedman, head of product at the company’s Superintelligence Labs. “They’ve been on an absolute tear, and I’m convinced MSL has the highest talent density of all the labs,” he added.
Meta confirmed the acquisition to TechCrunch but wouldn’t comment further or provide additional details about the deal.
Conductor, founded in 2024, only launched its core product just last summer. The company’s agentic teams, which can be deployed in the cloud, locally, or via a user’s phone, are designed to help software engineers work on separate, compartmentalized parts of a project in concert. The agents that the platform deploys aren’t developed in-house but come from major labs like Anthropic and OpenAI.
Holtz said that, until early next year, Conductor’s core features would continue to work as they previously have. The exception is Conductor’s cloud service, which will shut down on November 20, after which the company will begin deleting user cloud data.
Meta, which previously lagged behind in AI services, has spent the last several months trying to catch up. In August, the company launched Muse Code, its own coding agent. Meanwhile, the company’s recently launched Muse agents are seeing significant adoption, with the company recently reporting that the service had surpassed 10 million users. The company has also made a number of AI-related acquisitions over the past year, including Moltbook, the viral agent platform that made headlines.

report.summary: Meta acquires Conductor, an AI coding startup that orchestrates multiple agents in parallel workspaces, as Meta races to catch up in AI coding.
report.background: Conductor was founded in 2024 and only recently launched its core product: a platform that lets engineers deploy multiple AI agents into parallel, compartmentalized workspaces to work on different parts of a software project. It did not build its own models; instead it orchestrated agents from labs such as Anthropic and OpenAI. The deal comes as Meta tries to recover from a slow start in AI services. Meta launched its own coding agent, Muse Code, in August, and its Muse agents have passed 10 million users. It has also been acquiring AI startups, including Moltbook. AI coding has become one of the most competitive and commercially important battlegrounds, with large labs and startups racing to build agentic development tools.
key_points: Meta confirmed the acquisition but did not disclose terms. Conductor founder and CEO Charlie Holtz announced the move, saying the startup is joining Meta and teasing a new interface for early next year. Holtz said he looks forward to working with Meta chief AI officer Alexandr Wang and Nat Friedman of Superintelligence Labs.

Conductor's product deploys multiple AI agents into separate parallel workspaces so engineers can work on different parts of a project simultaneously. Agents can run in the cloud, locally, or via a phone. Conductor does not develop its own models; it uses agents from major labs including Anthropic and OpenAI, making it an orchestrator rather than a model maker.

Conductor's core features will keep working as before until early next year, but its cloud service will shut down on November 20. After that, Conductor will begin deleting user cloud data. The timeline gives users little time to export work or migrate to local or alternative setups, a key practical concern for teams relying on the cloud.

The deal fits Meta's broader push to catch up in AI. Meta launched Muse Code, its own coding agent, in August, and says its Muse agents have surpassed 10 million users. It previously acquired Moltbook and other AI startups. Buying Conductor gives Meta talent and experience in multi-agent coding interfaces as competition with OpenAI, Anthropic, and coding-tool startups intensifies.
report.impact: The acquisition signals further consolidation in agentic coding, where large labs are buying startups for talent and product know-how rather than building every workflow in-house. For Meta, Conductor could accelerate a new coding interface and help it compete with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Cursor-style tools. For developers, the immediate impact is disruption: Conductor cloud users must migrate before November 20 or lose data, and the product's long-term roadmap is uncertain. The bigger shift is toward parallel, multi-agent development workflows, which could raise productivity but also create new complexity around orchestration, permissions, and reliance on third-party models. Regular users may eventually see more capable coding assistants and app-building agents, though mostly indirectly through products built by developers.
report.tools: Readers can watch Meta's Muse Code and Conductor's local features until early next year. For open-source multi-agent coding, try OpenHands and Aider; also consider Claude Code or OpenAI Codex CLI for agent-backed development, and Cursor as a leading IDE alternative. If you use Conductor Cloud, export or back up data before November 20.
